title: Function-sparing cure of H3 K27-altered diffuse midline glioma

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a durable cure of childhood H3 K27-altered diffuse midline glioma, with particular emphasis on tumors in the pons, while preserving essential brainstem function. Success would mean that children survive long term without recurrent tumor and retain abilities such as breathing, protecting their airway, swallowing and moving independently. Tumor shrinkage alone would not establish this capability. This is a proposed therapeutic goal, not an achievement demonstrated by the supplied evidence.

The disease definitions matter. Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma, or DIPG, is a radiographic and anatomical diagnosis; H3 K27-altered pontine diffuse midline glioma specifies a molecularly defined tumor in that location; and H3 K27M-mutant diffuse midline glioma is the molecular definition used in the supplied FDA approval. These populations overlap but are not interchangeable. In particular, historical outcomes in a radiographically diagnosed DIPG registry cannot be assigned without qualification to every molecular subgroup, and responses in a study that excluded DIPG cannot establish cure of pontine disease.

significance.text: The historical DIPG outcomes explain the scale of the proposed advance. Hoffman and colleagues reported median survival of 11 months and five-year survival of 2.2% in a registry cohort of 1,008 eligible children and young adults. Those results document exceptionally poor survival, while also showing that long-term survival was not literally absent. The cohort was not uniformly confirmed to have H3 K27-altered tumors, so it provides important historical context rather than an exact molecularly matched prognosis for this concept.

Conditional impact assessment: a treatment that durably eliminated these pontine tumors while preserving swallowing, breathing and motor function would enable long-term survival with essential neurological abilities. Preserving function is central to the innovation: survival accompanied by severe permanent loss of brainstem function would represent a materially different outcome. The ambition is comparable to the transformation associated with durable childhood-leukemia cures, but that analogy concerns the scale of clinical change, not equivalent biology, treatment mechanisms or an assured path to success.

Conditional downstream possibilities are broader than the direct benefit but require separate discoveries. A successful approach might inform treatment of other developmental tumors, delivery of therapies within the central nervous system or protection of neurological function during cancer treatment. None of those extensions follows automatically from curing this tumor. A universal, non-toxic cure for childhood leukemia and solid tumors is outside this concept, and the supplied evidence does not establish comparative population burden against conditions such as prematurity or stunting.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability proposed here is sustained elimination or control of the tumor sufficient to prevent recurrence, together with preservation of the brainstem functions threatened by disease and treatment. The supplied dordaviprone evidence demonstrates responses in a selected recurrent population that excluded DIPG; it does not demonstrate this combined outcome in children with newly diagnosed pontine disease. This identifies the gap between the documented result and the proposed capability without claiming that the supplied material comprehensively establishes the treatment landscape in November 2026.

Engineering synthesis: a successful regimen would need an effective means of dealing with tumor throughout its clinically relevant extent, including disease that persists beyond an apparent imaging response. It would also need to prevent residual disease from causing recurrence while avoiding unacceptable injury to essential neural circuits. These requirements raise questions about treatment distribution, selectivity, resistance, local toxicity and the relationship between tumor control and neurological recovery. They do not require that an administered drug directly contact every malignant cell; indirect effects or combinations could, in principle, contribute to durable control.

Mechanistic uncertainty remains important. The earlier research proposed reversing an oncohistone-driven developmental arrest or killing cells maintained in that state. That is a possible mechanistic framing, but the supplied reviewed texts do not establish the mechanism, its necessity for cure or whether reversing it would be sufficient. The concept therefore remains open to different therapeutic routes. Likewise, assertions that radiotherapy slows growth, that it is the backbone of care or that these tumors cannot be surgically removed are not established by the retained evidence and are not used here as resolved premises.

Measurement is another barrier to demonstrating the capability. A convincing result must distinguish a temporary response from sustained disease control and must measure neurological function independently of tumor imaging. Long survival and complete radiographic remission are important observations, but neither alone proves that all tumor has been eradicated. Functional assessments must also distinguish abilities preserved throughout treatment from abilities regained after disease-related injury.

current_state.text: Hoffman and colleagues’ Journal of Clinical Oncology study was published online on May 10, 2018, with print publication on July 1, 2018; its DOI is 10.1200/JCO.2017.75.9308. After exclusions, the registry analysis included 1,008 children and young adults with radiographically confirmed DIPG. Median survival was 11 months, with an interquartile range of 7.5–16 months. Five-year survival was 2.2% (95% confidence interval, 1.4–3.4%), and 101 patients, or 10%, survived at least two years. The supplied review examined a PubMed abstract record with figure captions, not the full article; these numerical results were available in the retained text. The cohort was not uniformly molecularly characterized.

On August 6, 2025, the FDA granted accelerated approval to dordaviprone for adults and children aged one year and older with progressive H3 K27M-mutant diffuse midline glioma following prior therapy. The FDA described this as its first approval of a systemic therapy for that molecular definition. This is a documented regulatory milestone. Its indication must be distinguished from the narrower population that supplied the efficacy evidence.

In the integrated efficacy population of 50 patients, the FDA reported an overall response rate of 22% (95% confidence interval, 12–36%) and median response duration of 10.3 months (95% confidence interval, 7.3–15.2 months). This population excluded DIPG, primary spinal tumors, atypical histologies and cerebrospinal fluid dissemination. These responses support activity in the selected population; they do not establish durable complete remission, survival measured in years or preserved brainstem function in classic pontine disease. The cohort’s exclusions should not be presented as exclusions from the approval indication itself. The reviewed source was the complete FDA approval notice, not a full clinical study report.

The research also cited a November 2026 review in Critical Reviews in Oncology/Hematology, article 105574, and described access as abstract-only. However, the supplied source index contains no captured artifact, and the validated review had no retained text with which to verify its attributed statements. It therefore supplies no additional verified conclusion here about pontine efficacy or current treatment. No DOI is asserted for that article. This access limitation does not show that the article or its attributed conclusions are false.

The supplied evidence establishes the dated registry findings and the 2025 approval, but does not provide a comprehensive treatment assessment as of November 1, 2026. The bounded search record described in the review was empty. The warranted conclusion is that these documented results do not establish a function-sparing pontine cure; a categorical assertion that no such capability exists anywhere as of that date would exceed the supplied evidence.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: a multicenter cohort of children with newly diagnosed, centrally confirmed H3 K27-altered pontine diffuse midline glioma would receive a regimen that produces sustained complete radiographic and clinical remission in a majority, median overall survival measured in years and preservation of independent airway protection and ambulation in most survivors. Swallowing, breathing and motor outcomes would be assessed explicitly. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not established consensus thresholds for declaring cure.
completion_criteria.label: Majority complete remission, years-long median survival, and preserved brainstem function

completion_criteria.text: The protocol would prespecify the duration of follow-up, definitions of complete remission and recurrence, imaging methods, clinical assessments and handling of deaths or missing follow-up. It would report function both among survivors and relative to the original enrolled cohort, so that excellent function in a small surviving subset could not obscure poor overall outcomes. Baseline impairment, treatment-related injury, recovery, supportive-care needs and quality of life would help make the clinical meaning of preserved function assessable.
completion_criteria.label: Prespecified follow-up and outcomes with function reported against original enrollment

completion_criteria.text: Reproducibility proposal: results should be consistent across participating centers and subsequently confirmed in an independent cohort, with transparent eligibility criteria and central diagnostic and response review. A prespecified comparison against an appropriate contemporary control would strengthen claims of treatment benefit. The radiographically defined historical DIPG registry could supply context, but should not serve as an automatically equivalent molecularly matched control.
completion_criteria.label: Consistent multicenter results independently confirmed with central diagnostic and response review

completion_criteria.text: Practical boundaries would include the ages, molecular subgroups, tumor locations, disease stages and prior treatments actually studied, as well as treatment burden and persistent toxicity. Sustained remission over a defined observation period would establish demonstrated durability, not mathematical proof that recurrence is impossible. Even strong multicenter results would establish breadth within the tested population rather than universal effectiveness across all diffuse midline gliomas or childhood cancers.
completion_criteria.label: Report population boundaries, treatment burden, and limits of demonstrated durability

completion_criteria.text: The FDA-reported 22% response rate and median response duration of 10.3 months would not satisfy this proposal: they describe a minority response in a selected recurrent cohort that excluded DIPG, without establishing the proposed complete-remission, survival and functional outcomes in newly diagnosed pontine disease. This comparison clarifies the additional demonstration required without diminishing the significance of the approval.
completion_criteria.label: Complete-remission, survival, and functional outcomes beyond recurrent non-DIPG response evidence

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: PED-04, Controlled reopening of developmental critical periods, and PED-09, Post-symptomatic restoration of severe genetic neurodevelopmental disorders, overlap with PED-10 in questions about developmental state and neurological function. Their central goals are renewed plasticity or restoration of impaired development; PED-10 requires durable control of a malignancy. Reversing a developmental state cannot be assumed to cure the tumor, and eliminating the tumor cannot be assumed to restore established neurological injury.

Roster-based synthesis: PED-05, Prevention of cerebral palsy after perinatal brain injury, shares the goal of protecting long-term neurological function. Its initiating problem is perinatal injury, whereas PED-10 must combine cancer control with protection of brainstem abilities. PED-03, Reversal of established childhood stunting and its cognitive cost, also concerns developmental recovery, but recovery from stunting and survival after a brainstem malignancy remain distinct capabilities.

Roster-based synthesis: PED-06, Prenatal correction that lets severe monogenic disease develop normally, and PED-11, One-time in vivo correction of severe newborn metabolic disease before irreversible injury, share an interest in intervening before permanent damage. Their proposed correction of inherited disease does not establish a treatment for an existing tumor. PED-10 also does not inherently require prenatal intervention, gene correction or a one-time course.

Roster-based synthesis: PED-02, Protective adaptive immunity generated by the newborn; PED-12, Drug-free donor-specific tolerance for pediatric solid-organ grafts; and PED-13, Drug-free reset of severe pediatric autoimmune disease, concern different forms of immune function or regulation. An eventual immune-based treatment for PED-10 could create technical overlap, but no such mechanism is established by the supplied evidence. Antitumor control, protective immunity, graft tolerance and autoimmune remission are separate endpoints.

Roster-based synthesis: PED-01, Physiological extrauterine support through fetal organ maturity; PED-07, A physiological subpulmonary ventricle for single-ventricle heart disease; and PED-08, Restoration of nephron endowment after the nephrogenic clock stops, share the broader ambition of enabling survival with sustained organ function. Their support or restoration of developing organs does not subsume PED-10’s tumor-control requirement. Each remains a distinct innovation with its own convincing demonstration.

change_log.change: Preserved PED-10’s identity and function-sparing cure goal while making its pontine emphasis explicit.
change_log.reason: The concept remains coherent despite uncertainty in some supporting background assertions.

change_log.change: Separated radiographic DIPG, H3 K27-altered pontine tumors and the H3 K27M-mutant FDA indication.
change_log.reason: These overlapping populations cannot be treated as diagnostically or evidentially interchangeable.

change_log.reason: The registry reported five-year survival of 2.2%, so literal uniform fatality is not supported.

change_log.reason: These details are supported by the retained abstract and clarify the historical distribution of outcomes.

change_log.change: Expanded the dordaviprone account to include age eligibility, prior therapy, response-duration confidence interval and all supplied efficacy-cohort exclusions.
change_log.reason: These details define the scope of the demonstrated result and distinguish the approval indication from its evidence population.

change_log.change: Reframed direct contact with every infiltrative cell and reversal of developmental arrest as unestablished mechanistic requirements.
change_log.reason: The reviewed evidence does not establish their necessity, and a successful treatment could act through other routes.

change_log.reason: The supplied reviewed texts do not substantiate those assertions; that limitation does not establish their falsity.

change_log.reason: They explain the ambition without asserting biological equivalence or automatic extension to other cancers.

change_log.change: Replaced categorical present-day nonachievement with the narrower conclusion that the supplied results do not demonstrate the proposed cure.
change_log.reason: The evidence does not provide a comprehensive November 2026 treatment assessment.

change_log.reason: No retained text or captured artifact was available to the validated review.

change_log.change: Operationalized proposed completion criteria with follow-up, functional denominators, independent confirmation and practical boundaries.
change_log.reason: These additions make the proposal assessable while avoiding an unsupported consensus definition or proof of universal cure.

change_log.change: Added distinctions across the supplied roster as explicitly labeled synthesis.

unresolved_issues: The supplied material does not establish the complete treatment landscape or whether a function-sparing pontine cure remains unachieved as of November 1, 2026.
The November 2026 review’s contents, publication timing relative to the assessment date and DOI remain unverified because no retained text was supplied.
The role of oncohistone-driven developmental arrest, and whether reversing it is necessary or sufficient for cure, remains unresolved in the supplied evidence.

The proportion of radiographic DIPG that belongs to the target molecular group, surgical unresectability, radiotherapy’s role and comparative population burden are not established by the retained texts.

The reviewed FDA notice does not establish dordaviprone’s efficacy or functional outcomes in classic pontine disease; exclusion from its efficacy cohort is not evidence of ineffectiveness in that population.

A future protocol must define sustained remission, follow-up duration, functional thresholds, diagnostic eligibility and an appropriate comparator. The proposed thresholds are not established standards of cure.
The extent to which tumor control could preserve existing function or restore function already lost to disease remains undetermined.

brief.title: A childhood brain cancer cure that preserves vital abilities
possible: Children with H3 K27-altered diffuse midline glioma, a brain cancer defined by changes in tumor cells, could survive long term without the cancer returning. For tumors in the pons, a part of the brainstem, they could keep the ability to breathe, swallow safely and move independently.
why: For children and their families, this would mean lasting survival with essential abilities preserved. In a historical study of tumors diagnosed by scans in the pons, median survival was just 11 months.

sources.showed: Their registry study found very short survival in children and young adults with diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma, or DIPG, a tumor diagnosed by its location in the pons and appearance on scans. Some patients survived long term.
sources.cited_for: The study establishes the historical scale of the survival challenge.
sources.not_established: The tumors were not all molecularly characterized, so these outcomes do not give an exact prognosis for the target cancer.

sources.showed: The FDA reported tumor responses to dordaviprone and granted accelerated approval for previously treated, worsening disease with the H3 K27M mutation, a specific molecular change.
sources.quote: Among the 11 patients with objective responses,
sources.cited_for: Dordaviprone has demonstrated activity in a selected group with recurrent disease.
sources.not_established: The efficacy group excluded DIPG and did not establish lasting cure with preserved brainstem function.

shown: The FDA reported that dordaviprone produced tumor responses in 22% of a selected group with recurrent disease. The trials had no randomly assigned comparison group. They demonstrate treatment activity; lasting remission with preserved brainstem function in children with newly diagnosed pontine tumors remains to be demonstrated.
missing: A treatment must prevent recurrence while preserving breathing, safe swallowing and independent movement.
Trials must measure neurological abilities separately from tumor scans and distinguish preserved abilities from recovered ones.
Independent groups must reproduce lasting remission and survival benefits in children with the target pontine cancer.

milestones.label: Lasting complete remission with vital abilities preserved
milestones.explanation: A study across hospitals would need complete remission in most children, median survival measured in years and essential abilities preserved in most survivors. This would establish the combined survival and function benefit.

milestones.label: Clear follow-up and outcomes for everyone enrolled
milestones.explanation: A trial would need predefined follow-up and outcome rules, with function reported for survivors and everyone originally enrolled. This would prevent good outcomes in a small surviving group from obscuring deaths.

milestones.label: Consistent results confirmed by an independent study
milestones.explanation: Results would need to agree across hospitals and an independent group, with shared expert review of diagnoses and responses. A suitable contemporary comparison would strengthen the claim of treatment benefit.

milestones.label: Clear limits on benefit, burden and durability
milestones.explanation: Studies would need to report who benefited, treatment burden, lasting harm and how long remission persisted. This would define the demonstrated benefit without implying that recurrence is impossible.

milestones.label: Cure outcomes beyond the existing tumor response results
milestones.explanation: Treatment would need to establish complete remission, long survival and preserved function in newly diagnosed pontine disease. Responses in the selected recurrent group treated with dordaviprone do not establish those outcomes.

uncertain: The follow-up duration and functional thresholds needed to judge cure remain to be defined.
It remains unclear how much treatment could restore abilities already lost to the tumor.
Whether reversing the tumor cells’ arrested development is necessary or sufficient for cure remains unresolved.

page.title: Cure of H3 K27-altered pontine diffuse midline glioma
page.definition: Children with H3 K27-altered diffuse midline glioma centred in the pons, part of the brainstem, survive after treatment without recurrence while breathing unassisted, swallowing safely and walking independently. Imaging can identify a diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG). The molecular diagnosis requires loss of the three-methyl-group mark on lysine 27 of histone H3, a DNA-packaging protein. A K27M mutation or excess EZHIP protein can cause this loss.

goal.need: Among 1,008 children and young adults with DIPG diagnosed by imaging, median survival was 11 months and estimated five-year survival was 2.2% (95% CI, 1.4–3.4%). Radiotherapy temporarily eases or stabilises symptoms in about 70% of patients. Higher doses have not prolonged survival. In a London cohort of 63 children, 90% had impaired mobility, 83% had difficulty swallowing and 78% had difficulty breathing in their last 12 weeks of life. A cure that spares the brainstem would let children survive with these abilities intact.

figures.caption: Historical survival in radiographically confirmed DIPG
figures.note: Diagnoses spanned 1990–2015; the cohort was not uniformly confirmed as H3 K27-altered.

completion.title: Independent cohorts reproduce five-year complete remission with breathing, swallowing and walking preserved.
completion.criterion: A regimen produces complete remission lasting at least 5 years in children with molecularly confirmed H3 K27-altered pontine diffuse midline glioma, with no ongoing tumour-directed treatment at assessment. Unassisted breathing, safe oral swallowing and independent ambulation remain preserved, without persistent treatment-related loss of these abilities. The combined outcome is reproduced in an independent prospective cohort. Five years is borrowed from NCI's general remission convention; it is not a validated DMG cure threshold.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis; no outside body located specifies this combined cure-and-function test.
completion.basis: RAPNO defines complete response in DIPG. NCI describes five years in complete remission as a general cancer convention and acknowledges the possibility of later recurrence. The five years run from the first documented complete remission. BIOMEDE 2.0 measures progression-free survival from randomisation for its internal comparison. The requirements for function, treatment status at assessment and independent replication belong to the Atlas composite.

milestones.title: A candidate treatment shows efficacy in multiple relevant DMG models in culture and in animals.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate antitumour activity in multiple models relevant to the intended pontine DMG population, including both cell and animal models. Select models and endpoints suited to the tumour biology and the agent. Justify the number and choice of models where few relevant models exist.
milestones.set_by: CONNECT, PNOC and ITCC-Brain networks, 2023 preclinical translation guidelines for childhood brain tumours.
milestones.threshold_quote: Efficacy in multiple relevant models in vitro and in vivo

milestones.title: A phase 1 trial identifies an intravenous GD2-CAR T-cell dose targeting ≤30% dose-limiting toxicity.
milestones.criterion: Under NCT04196413 arm A, identify a maximum tolerated or recommended phase 2 intravenous dose of GD2-directed CAR T cells after lymphodepletion. Use 3+3 dose escalation and count protocol-defined dose-limiting toxicities at least possibly attributable to the infusion within 28 days. The target rate is ≤30%. Pontine safety data govern escalation for patients with pontine disease.
milestones.set_by: Stanford University, NCT04196413 arm A protocol, reported by Monje and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: The targeted DLT rate was 30% or less.

milestones.title: Pontine DMG disappears on MRI for ≥8 weeks with stable or improving neurological examination.
milestones.criterion: Brain and spine MRI show no enhancing or non-enhancing disease, measurable or non-measurable, for at least 8 weeks, with no new lesions. The neurological examination is stable or improving. The child is off antiangiogenic drugs and off steroids except for physiological replacement. If the spine was clear at baseline, a complete brain response requires repeat spine MRI to confirm clearance throughout the neuraxis.
milestones.set_by: Response Assessment in Pediatric Neuro-Oncology working group, 2020 DIPG recommendations, Table 2.
milestones.threshold_quote: maintained for ≥8 weeks; no new lesions

milestones.title: A randomised study shows longer survival in pontine DMG with an acceptable toxicity profile.
milestones.criterion: In a randomised controlled study of pontine DMG, the regimen produces a statistically significant improvement in overall survival compared with the control arm, with an acceptable toxicity profile. Measure overall survival from randomisation to death from any cause and analyse patients in their assigned groups.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Clinical Trial Endpoints for the Approval of Cancer Drugs and Biologics, 2018, section III.A; general oncology guidance.
milestones.threshold_quote: Demonstration of a statistically significant improvement in overall survival can be considered to be clinically significant if the toxicity profile is acceptable

milestones.title: A child with pontine DMG remains in complete remission for at least 5 years.
milestones.criterion: A child with molecularly confirmed H3 K27-altered pontine DMG remains continuously in complete remission for at least five years from the first documented complete remission. Five years is a general cancer convention described by NCI. Later recurrence remains possible.
milestones.set_by: National Cancer Institute, Cancer Prognosis, reviewed on 29 May 2024; a general cancer remission convention, not a DMG-specific cure definition.
milestones.threshold_quote: If you remain in complete remission for 5 years or more, some doctors may say that you are cured.

milestones.title: The candidate agent reaches pontine tumour tissue at a clinically relevant dose.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate penetration of the agent into pontine tumour tissue at a dose relevant to clinical use. The evidence may come from the proposed study or existing distribution data for the agent.
milestones.set_by: CONNECT, PNOC and ITCC-Brain networks, 2023 guidelines for preclinical assessment, Table 1.
milestones.threshold_quote: Data showing penetration into tumour tissue at clinically relevant doses

results.finding: In the phase 1 DMG trial, 0 of 3 patients had dose-limiting toxicity at the maximum tolerated IV dose.
results.detail: Of 13 enrolled, 11 were treated: nine had pontine DMG and two had spinal DMG. The maximum tolerated dose was 1×10^6 cells/kg; at 3×10^6 cells/kg, 3 of 8 had dose-limiting toxicity. Escalation used a 3+3 design and a 28-day assessment window. These are dose-finding results, not evidence of cure.
results.quote: No dose-limiting toxicities occurred on DL1, but three patients experienced dose-limiting cytokine release syndrome on DL2, establishing DL1 as the maximally tolerated IV dose.

results.finding: Among 11 patients treated with GD2-CAR T cells, 1 patient with pontine DMG had a complete response.
results.detail: The response remained ongoing at 30 months after enrolment and was accompanied by neurological improvement. The paper reports a RANO 2.0 response, but does not establish every RAPNO requirement, including brain and spine MRI findings and medication restrictions.
results.quote: This complete response was sustained at 30 months following enrolment, the time of data cut-off, and is ongoing

results.finding: Nine treated patients with pontine DMG had median overall survival of 17.6 months from diagnosis.
results.detail: This was a single-arm phase I study, not a randomised comparison. All nine patients with DIPG developed tumour inflammation-associated neurotoxicity after IV infusion, including two grade 4 events.
results.quote: For patients with DIPG, median overall survival was 17.6 months and for sDMG was 31.96 months

results.finding: One 17-year-old patient with pontine DMG had a complete response at 30 months after enrolment.
results.detail: The response began after enrolment, so 30 months is not its duration. The patient received repeated CAR T-cell infusions; five years of complete remission was not established.
results.quote: This complete response was sustained at 30 months following enrolment, the time of data cut-off, and is ongoing

results.finding: ONC201 plus paxalisib prolonged survival versus vehicle in all 3 pontine DIPG xenograft models and inhibited growth in patient-derived cultures.
results.detail: The magnitude of benefit varied by model. In SF8628, reported survival was 28 days with either the combination or paxalisib alone.
results.quote: combined treatment tested in two out of three DIPG xenograft models significantly extended the survival of mice compared with monotherapies, whereas the combination had an additive effect in the other.

results.finding: Two pontine DIPG xenograft models showed tumour pharmacodynamic changes after oral ONC201 and paxalisib dosing.
results.detail: The study sampled SU-DIPG-VI/Luc tumours after two weeks and HSJD-DIPG-007 tumours after four weeks.
results.quote:
showed increased Akt phosphorylation and expression of EZH2 following ONC201 treatment alone, consistent with our
in vitro
proteomic profiling, with the former rescued using paxalisib

results.finding: In 2 children with H3 K27M pontine DMG, the largest MRI tumour-area reduction was 80.3% from diagnosis, with residual tumour.
results.detail: Both children received radiation, which may have contributed to regression. The second child received concomitant steroids.
results.quote: Both patients demonstrated resolution of clinical symptoms and radiographic tumor regression.

results.finding: After intracerebroventricular B7-H3 CAR T dosing for DIPG, CAR T cells were detected in cerebrospinal fluid in 13 of 18 evaluable patients.
results.detail: Flow cytometry detected the EGFRt transduction tag in serial cerebrospinal fluid samples. The sampled compartment was cerebrospinal fluid.
results.quote:
B7-H3 CAR T cells were detected via their EGFRt transduction tag in 38.1% (40 of 105) of CSF biospecimens in courses 1 and 2 (Extended Data Figs.
2
and
3
and
Supplementary Table
) with 13 of 18 (72%) evaluable patients having detectable CAR T cells in at least one timepoint.

results.finding: Among 18 MRI-evaluable patients with DIPG treated with intracerebroventricular B7-H3 CAR T cells, one had a partial response.
results.detail: The authors considered resolution of radiation-induced pseudoprogression a possible explanation for the partial response.
results.quote: The best individual neuroimaging responses on MRI were 1 partial response (PR; 6%), 15 stable disease (SD; 83%) and 2 PD (11%).

results.finding: Among 21 patients with DIPG treated with intracerebroventricular B7-H3 CAR T cells, median survival from diagnosis was 19.8 months.
results.detail: Variable time from diagnosis to enrolment and changes in supportive care and re-irradiation limit the historical comparison.
results.quote:

) and the median time from diagnosis to death (or last contact for survivors) was 19.8 months

results.finding: Among four long-term survivors with H3 K27M-mutant pontine DMG, one had complete clearance of the tumour-related brain MRI signal.
results.detail: The follow-up scan for BIOMEDE 143 showed two punctate T2 signals attributed to the biopsy scar.
results.quote: Three showed residual MRI abnormalities at the last evaluation, whereas one achieved complete remission with clearance of all TP53-mutant fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) hypersignals (Extended Data Fig.  7a ).

results.finding: In randomized DIPG (n=193 in the pairwise comparison), everolimus versus dasatinib yielded an overall survival hazard ratio of 0.89.
results.detail: Toxicity led to discontinuation in 3% with everolimus versus 14% with dasatinib. Comparisons with the 66 historical controls also found no significant survival advantage and measured survival from biopsy.
results.quote: The trial did not show any significant OS difference (Fig.  2a–d  and Extended Data Table  2 ).

results.finding: Among four long-term survivors with H3 K27M-mutant pontine DMG, one had complete remission at follow-up.
results.detail: The six-year interval begins at diagnosis. The paper does not give the age of the patient with complete remission.
results.quote: Three showed residual MRI abnormalities at the last evaluation, whereas one achieved complete remission with clearance of all TP53-mutant fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) hypersignals (Extended Data Fig.  7a ).

results.finding: B-SYNC T cells showed antitumour activity after 1 infusion in immunodeficient DMG models. Group sizes unreported.
results.detail: The immunocompetent model used a different CAR construct. Intracerebroventricular delivery of the B-SYNC-B/I variant caused fatal neurotoxicity in immunodeficient models.
results.quote: In immunodeficient DMG models, a single infusion of intravenous (iv) or intracerebroventricular (icv) B-SYNC circuit T cells led to tumor infiltration, sustained persistence, antitumor activity, and extended survival.

results.finding: B-SYNC T cells infiltrated tumours after 1 infusion in immunodeficient DMG models. Group sizes unreported.
results.quote: In immunodeficient DMG models, a single infusion of intravenous (iv) or intracerebroventricular (icv) B-SYNC circuit T cells led to tumor infiltration, sustained persistence, antitumor activity, and extended survival.

results.finding: B7-H3 CAR T cells plus ONC206 increased killing in five DIPG cultures and prolonged survival in SU-DIPG-XIII xenografts to up to 101 days (n=12 in the combination arm).
results.detail: The PBT-29FH survival trend favoured the combination, but the text and figure caption give different maximum survival times for that model.
results.quote: In vivo combinatorial studies of ONC206 and a single ICV dose of B7-H3 CAR T cells extended survival in DIPG xenograft mouse models.

results.finding: In the SU-DIPG-13 xenograft group given CXCR3-A-modified B7-H3 CAR T cells intracerebroventricularly (n=6), tumour bioluminescence fell to background within 7 days.
results.detail: One treated SU-DIPG-13 mouse had residual tumour on histology despite a background imaging signal. Low B7-H3 expression and loss of luciferase suggested antigen escape and explained why imaging missed the tumour.
results.quote: When the CAR T cells were locoregionally delivered via ICV injection, the CAR-3A T cells reduced the tumor signals to the background level within 7 days

results.finding: CXCR3-A-modified B7-H3 CAR T cells were detected in SU-DIPG-13 tumour areas by 24 hours after intracerebroventricular delivery (n=2 mice per group per time point).
results.detail: The tissue readout was qualitative. The cited clinical experience used standard B7-H3 CAR T cells.
results.quote: there appeared to be greater abundance of CXCL10 at the tumor sites where the ICV delivered CAR-3A T cells had efficiently trafficked to within 24 hours

results.finding: In the 12-patient H3K27M-mutant DMG cohort, GD2-CAR T cells typically made up <10% of cerebrospinal fluid T cells after the sixth infusion.
results.detail: Treatment began with one intravenous infusion after lymphodepletion, followed by repeated intracerebroventricular infusions in eligible patients. The study also sampled an intratumoral cyst but gives no explicit CAR T-cell result for those samples.
results.quote: the data demonstrate poor persistence of GD2-CAR T cells within the CSF following one IV and sequential ICV GD2-CAR T cell infusions

results.finding: One of 11 on-study GD2-CAR T-cell recipients had an ongoing complete response with reversal of neurological deficits.
results.detail: The report measures follow-up from therapy initiation and gives no dates for brain and spine scans documenting the required eight weeks of clearance.
results.quote: one patient experienced an ongoing complete response associated with reversal of neurologic deficits

results.finding: Pt10, one of 11 on-study GD2-CAR T-cell recipients, had an ongoing complete response more than four years after starting therapy.
results.detail: The date of first documented complete remission is unspecified.
results.quote: Pt10 continues to manifest an ongoing durable complete response more than four years since beginning therapy.

results.finding: Tumour inflammation-associated neurotoxicity followed intravenous GD2-CAR T-cell infusion in all 9 patients with DIPG.
results.detail: Local inflammation is an indirect marker of tumour engagement. The study assayed CAR T cells in blood and cerebrospinal fluid.
results.quote: Nine of nine (100%) patients with DIPG developed TIAN following IV GD2-CART

results.finding: Among 11 intravenous GD2-CAR T-cell recipients, 1 × 10⁶ cells/kg was the maximum tolerated dose.
results.quote: No dose-limiting toxicities occurred on DL1, but three patients experienced dose-limiting cytokine release syndrome on DL2, establishing DL1 as the maximally tolerated IV dose.

results.finding: One child with H3K27M pontine DMG had an ongoing brain MRI complete response at 30 months after enrolment, with neurological improvement.
results.detail: The authors classified the response as complete under RANO 2.0. Serial brain MRI showed stable biopsy-tract signal and subtle medullary T2 hyperintensity of unclear significance.
results.quote: One patient exhibited a complete response ongoing for over 30 months since enrolment.

results.finding: In 9 treated patients with H3K27M pontine DMG, median overall survival from diagnosis was 17.6 months.
results.detail: The authors considered a historical-control comparison infeasible because the cohort was highly selected.

results.finding: One child with molecularly confirmed H3K27M pontine DMG remained in complete response at 30 months after enrolment.
results.quote: One patient exhibited a complete response ongoing for over 30 months since enrolment.

results.finding: Among four very-long-term survivors with H3-K27M pontine DMG, one had MRI FLAIR clearance.
results.detail: The authors described the survivors as having no meaningful sequelae, but gave no serial neurological examination findings for the patient with MRI clearance.

results.finding: In 1 patient with H3K27M-mutated DIPG, GD2-CAR T cells reached pontine tumour tissue after an intravenous dose of 1 × 10⁶ cells/kg.
results.detail: Direct pontine tissue evidence came from a single autopsy. The patient’s tumour progressed despite treatment.

results.finding: In one child with H3K27M-mutant pontine diffuse midline glioma, gemcitabine averaged 7.65 µM across four tumour biopsy cores.
results.detail: Two children were enrolled based on MRI findings. One had H3K27M-mutant diffuse midline glioma, and the other had H3K27-wildtype low-grade glioma.
results.quote: In a phase 0 clinical trial of i.v. gemcitabine prior to biopsy in children newly diagnosed with DIPG by MRI, mean concentration in 4 biopsy cores in patient 1 (H3K27M diffuse midline glioma) was 7.65 µM.

results.finding: In 45 DIPG patients given intratumoral ¹²⁴I-omburtamab, mean initial PET/CT uptake in the lesion was 49% of injected activity.
results.detail: The 49% is the fraction of injected activity measured in the lesion. Tumour coverage was not quantified by that measure.
results.quote: The mean lesion uptake was 49 ± 18 percent injected dose as measured from the initial imaging and ranging as high as 99%.

definition = "Children with H3 K27-altered diffuse midline glioma centred in the pons, part of the brainstem, survive after treatment without recurrence while breathing unassisted, swallowing safely and walking independently. Imaging can identify a diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (DIPG). The molecular diagnosis requires loss of the three-methyl-group mark on lysine 27 of histone H3, a DNA-packaging protein. A K27M mutation or excess EZHIP protein can cause this loss.". Reason: The definition needs to identify the precise histone mark and distinguish the molecular diagnosis from the diagnosis made by imaging.

goal.need = "Among 1,008 children and young adults with DIPG diagnosed by imaging, median survival was 11 months and estimated five-year survival was 2.2% (95% CI, 1.4\u20133.4%). Radiotherapy temporarily eases or stabilises symptoms in about 70% of patients. Higher doses have not prolonged survival. In a London cohort of 63 children, 90% had impaired mobility, 83% had difficulty swallowing and 78% had difficulty breathing in their last 12 weeks of life. A cure that spares the brainstem would let children survive with these abilities intact.". Reason: The registry survival figures gain clinical meaning from the limits of radiotherapy and the measured frequency of losing mobility, swallowing and breathing function.

add statement by Australian Government, Minister for Health and Aged Care, 2024: "find treatments and a cure for DIPG and childhood brain cancer.". Reason: The minister names cure directly, and the announcement also identifies quality of life and survival as programme aims.

edit completion: basis = "RAPNO defines complete response in DIPG. NCI describes five years in complete remission as a general cancer convention and acknowledges the possibility of later recurrence. The five years run from the first documented complete remission. BIOMEDE 2.0 measures progression-free survival from randomisation for its internal comparison. The requirements for function, treatment status at assessment and independent replication belong to the Atlas composite."; refs = [2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 21]. Reason: The basis can distinguish the time origin of remission from the endpoints actually registered in BIOMEDE 2.0.

edit m1: title = "A candidate treatment shows efficacy in multiple relevant DMG models in culture and in animals."; criterion = "Demonstrate antitumour activity in multiple models relevant to the intended pontine DMG population, including both cell and animal models. Select models and endpoints suited to the tumour biology and the agent. Justify the number and choice of models where few relevant models exist."; threshold_quote = "Efficacy in multiple relevant models in vitro and in vivo"; threshold_ref = 9; refs = [9, 10]. Reason: The networks accept several measures of efficacy, and the mouse study's results obscure their actual prioritisation criterion.

add milestone after m1: "The candidate agent reaches pontine tumour tissue at a clinically relevant dose.". Reason: The preclinical guidelines separately ask whether an agent can reach tumour tissue at a dose relevant to patients.

edit m2: title = "A phase 1 trial identifies an intravenous GD2-CAR T-cell dose targeting \u226430% dose-limiting toxicity."; criterion = "Under NCT04196413 arm A, identify a maximum tolerated or recommended phase 2 intravenous dose of GD2-directed CAR T cells after lymphodepletion. Use 3+3 dose escalation and count protocol-defined dose-limiting toxicities at least possibly attributable to the infusion within 28 days. The target rate is \u226430%. Pontine safety data govern escalation for patients with pontine disease."; threshold_quote = "The targeted DLT rate was 30% or less."; threshold_ref = 11; refs = [11]. Reason: The 30% target applies to intravenous GD2-CAR T-cell dose escalation in a specific protocol, whose pontine safety decision had a site-specific rule.

edit m3: criterion = "Brain and spine MRI show no enhancing or non-enhancing disease, measurable or non-measurable, for at least 8 weeks, with no new lesions. The neurological examination is stable or improving. The child is off antiangiogenic drugs and off steroids except for physiological replacement. If the spine was clear at baseline, a complete brain response requires repeat spine MRI to confirm clearance throughout the neuraxis."; set_by = "Response Assessment in Pediatric Neuro-Oncology working group, 2020 DIPG recommendations, Table 2."; threshold_quote = "maintained for \u22658 weeks; no new lesions"; threshold_ref = 7; refs = [7]. Reason: RAPNO Table 2 supplies the missing threshold quotation and specifies when spinal imaging confirms a complete brain response.

edit m4: criterion = "In a randomised controlled study of pontine DMG, the regimen produces a statistically significant improvement in overall survival compared with the control arm, with an acceptable toxicity profile. Measure overall survival from randomisation to death from any cause and analyse patients in their assigned groups."; refs = [5]. Reason: FDA defines the survival clock and analysis population, whereas the BIOMEDE and dordaviprone findings are study outcomes.

Reason: Counting from the first documented complete remission prevents five-year survival from diagnosis from being scored as five years in remission.
